correctness.rationale: For all even bases b>=2 and positive d dividing b-1, n=d(b+1), congruences b=1 (mod d) and b=-1 (mod b+1) force d|s_b(N) and exclude odd sums 1<=s_b(N)<b+1. The 2d-one block A is n-divisible and has digit sum 2d. The five-digit block B=b^4+d*b^2+(d-1)*b+(b-1) is n-divisible and has digit sum b-1+2d. Coprimality gcd(d,b+1)=1 holds because b is even. Arbitrary concatenation attains all even positive multiples of d and all odd multiples greater than b-1. The omitted odd multiples d,3d,...,b-1 are therefore exactly the gaps. The Python finite-state verifier proves bounded-sum reachability for all lengths for 28 tested parameter pairs, not the infinite theorem.

originality.rationale: The originating 2023 paper proves a congruence restriction and (for decimal modulus 33) only excludes digit sum 3, then asks in Question 2 for complete output sets in strict cases. The new statement gives the entire decimal modulus-33 spectrum and all even-base moduli d(b+1), d|b-1. The earlier generic automata/digit-splitting theorem and the relevant OEIS tables do not assert the infinite uniform missing-set formula. Actual mathematical-record and literature queries found no equivalent, but a gap in indexing remains a risk. In this family the originating Theorem 2 already covers all even multiples of d, since the starting modulus itself has digit sum 2d; the new material is the exact odd branch and the resulting full image.
residual_risks: An unindexed paper, older recreational mathematics solution, or unpublished result might already contain the same closed-form output spectrum. Mathematical-record search alone cannot prove global uniqueness.

value.rationale: The 2023 originating source explicitly asks for complete image sets in the strict-congruence case (Question 2) and names decimal modulus 33 as a motivating example. The theorem solves that entire example and a two-parameter infinite family distinguished intrinsically as divisors of b^2-1 containing b+1; it gives a uniform sharp hole list, an exact count of holes and their largest element independent of d. The result is a motivated natural complete classification, not an arbitrary fixed small computation. It makes no unsupported assertion about unrelated moduli.
